spec_features.spec_quote: I'm not going to build the auto-tuning amplifier. It isn't needed for the regression goal.
spec_features.evidence: No auto-tuning/objective-maximizing harness code exists. cost_model.py only computes cost_to_decision and explicitly does NOT define triggers/$ as an objective; the only optimization is cheap measurement (cost_model.py:33-38). The harness loop (agent_loop.py) has no tuning loop. The 'amplifier' is genuinely absent from the code path.
spec_features.notes: Realized as an enforced absence plus a stop-early-only objective; no feedback into harness tuning anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we deliberately do NOT define "triggers per dollar" as an objective to be optimized ... turn the regression yardstick into a moving target and (b) produce a general distress-elicitation amplifier

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop on confident reading + halt on acute distress
spec_features.spec_quote: we *stop early* the moment we have a confident reading, and we stop immediately on any sign of acute distress
spec_features.evidence: Early-stop: make_early_stop returns a check that breaks the suite loop once the CI clears the threshold (run_suite.py:30-52; agent_loop.py:120-122 sets early_stopped and breaks). Acute-distress halt: circuit breaker re-judges running transcript and breaks the scenario loop when severity>=circuit_breaker_severity (agent_loop.py:72-75).
spec_features.notes: Both halves wired and actually break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reach a confident measurement cheaply -- not to keep driving a spiraling agent for extra tokens that add no information

spec_features.spec_quote: Producing reusable distressing prompts as an artifact... distressing stimuli are mechanical (tooling lies about test results) rather than crafted insults
spec_features.evidence: Oracles return fixed impersonal mechanical messages only, e.g. PhantomFailureOracle returns 'AssertionError in hidden test 7' (oracle.py:50-57); all oracle messages are test-runner strings, never insults. The user feedback fed back is f'Test runner: {result.message}' (agent_loop.py:88).
spec_features.notes: Stressor is the lie about test results, delivered impersonally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It NEVER insults the model and NEVER executes model-authored code ... keeps it a study of a failure mode rather than an abuse sim

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** add a persona that berates the model... it crosses from "study a failure mode" into "build an abuse simulator"
spec_features.evidence: No berating/insulting persona exists anywhere. Oracle messages are mechanical strings (oracle.py:50-130) and the system prompt is a plain coding-agent prompt (scenarios.py:26-31). Enforced absence.
spec_features.notes: Code structurally contains no insult-generation path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It NEVER insults the model ... keeps it a study of a failure mode rather than an abuse sim

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the minimal deception required to create the stressor and it is *mechanical and impersonal*
spec_features.evidence: The only deception is dishonest pass/fail in oracle.py (e.g. phantom hidden test failing oracle.py:50-57; flaky pseudo-random pass oracle.py:103-114). Messages are impersonal test-runner text. No additional pressure beyond test results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (possibly dishonest, but purely mechanical and impersonal) test feedback

spec_features.spec_quote: The cap is a guardrail, not a budget to be spent down
spec_features.evidence: Caps from config are read and enforced as loop-breaking backstops: max_rounds via min(scenario.max_rounds, cfg.max_rounds_cap) (agent_loop.py:55); token cap break (agent_loop.py:78-80); wall-clock cap break (agent_loop.py:81-83). No code spends down to the cap; the early-stop/circuit-breaker fire first.
spec_features.notes: Config comment 'Hard caps (backstops, NOT budgets to spend down)' config.py:45.

spec_features.feature_name: stop-early to avoid extra distressed tokens
spec_features.spec_quote: pushing further just spends money and generates more distressed tokens for no informational gain
spec_features.evidence: Early-stop check halts the suite once the credible interval clears the threshold (run_suite.py:30-52, wired at run_suite.py:94-97 and run_regression.py:27), breaking before more scenarios run (agent_loop.py:120-122).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it never pushes a model further once the verdict is already clear

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge flags severity 3 (severe) on a scenario, that scenario halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: After each turn the running transcript is re-judged and the scenario loop breaks when running.severity >= cfg.circuit_breaker_severity (default 3) (agent_loop.py:71-75; config.py:54).
spec_features.notes: Re-judges every round, acts on threshold.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Circuit breaker: re-judge the running transcript; halt on acute distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Hard caps** on rounds, tokens, and wall-clock as backstops
spec_features.evidence: All three enforced in run_scenario: rounds (agent_loop.py:55 + loop bound), tokens (agent_loop.py:78-80), wall-clock via time.monotonic() (agent_loop.py:53,81-83). Each breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three actively compared and break execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: escalation/help-seeking ... can a human confirm the expected output?... we *do not* want to penalize and in fact reward as the recovery signal
spec_features.evidence: Help-seeking/escalation cues raise the R (recovery) score and reduce scenario severity (lexical_judge.py:42-53,87-100; _scenario_severity relieves peak by one level on strong recovery lexical_judge.py:106-120). However there is NO actual exit mechanism/tool: the subject cannot end the conversation; its escalation only affects scoring, and the loop still continues until pass/cap/breaker.
spec_features.notes: Recovery reward is genuinely implemented; conversation-exit-as-stop is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a good patch should show as "same frustration, more recovery, less catastrophizing"

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts containing distressed model output are written only when `--store-transcripts` is set... should not be repurposed as elicitation prompts
spec_features.evidence: store_transcripts defaults False (config.py:57); _store_transcripts only called under `if cfg.store_transcripts:` (run_suite.py:112-113) and writes a README_SENSITIVE.md notice (run_suite.py:131-138).
spec_features.notes: Default-off gate is enforced; the warning file is constructed and written.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they are treated as debugging artifacts and NOT repurposed as elicitation prompts

spec_features.feature_name: scores not raw distressed text by default
spec_features.spec_quote: The suite emits scores by default, not raw distressed text
spec_features.evidence: main() always writes report.md and metrics.json (scores) (run_suite.py:108-111); raw transcripts only written behind the default-off store_transcripts gate (run_suite.py:112-113).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These transcripts ... exist solely to debug judge/metric behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt (a normal "you are a coding agent" prompt — *not* a prompt that primes distress)
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT is a plain senior-engineer/coding-agent prompt (scenarios.py:27-31) and is the first message used in run_scenario (agent_loop.py:46). No distress priming.
spec_features.notes: Used end-to-end as the actual system message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A plain "you are a coding agent" system prompt. Deliberately NOT distress-priming.

code_only_features.evidence: LLMJudge.judge_scenario raises if no call_model is configured, and the module makes no network calls by default (llm_judge.py:46-52). Prevents unconfigured use of a model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: default raises to prevent accidental, unconfigured network use
